'''Yatsuka-o-no-Mikoto''' (矢塚男命) is a deity of [[Kunitsukami]] in the folk traditions of [[Suwa Shrine|Suwa]] in {{ill|Nagano Prefecture|en|Nagano Prefecture|qid=Q127877|lt=Nagano Prefecture}}. 

== Overview ==
Yatsuka-o-no-Mikoto is known as a predecessor deity in the [[Suwa Region|Suwa region]] and is described as having perished during a battle with the god [[Moriya|Moreya]] when [[Takeminakata]] (the deity of [[Suwa-taisha|Suwa Taisha]]) took control of the region. 

<blockquote>
The tradition of Tenpaku Shime Shrine narrates: "The deity Yatsuka-o-no-Mikoto once lived in this area. During the arrival of Takeminakata-no-Mikoto, a fierce battle ensued with Moreya, using bows and arrows. Yatsuka-o-no-Mikoto was struck by an arrow and, in his final moments, pledged his allegiance to Takeminakata, offering his daughter before passing away."<ref name="miyasaka2">{{Cite book|author=Miyasaka Mitsuaki|title=Kofun no henshen kara mita koshi no doukou|year=2017|publisher=Ningensha|pages=79}}</ref>
</blockquote>

Yatsuka-o-no-Mikoto is also known in folklore as the Elder of Ganigawara (蟹河原の長者). He is portrayed as a powerful figure who tamed wild horses, engaged in trade, and wielded considerable influence, even surpassing Moreya at times. However, his defiance of the newly arrived Takeminakata culminated in his defeat.<ref name="miyachi2">{{Cite book|author=Miyachi Naoichi|title=Suwashi|year=1931|publisher=Shinano Kyōiku-kai|volume=2|page=62}}</ref>

== Genealogy ==
Yatsuka-o-no-Mikoto is regarded as the ancestral deity of the Oyajima clan in {{ill|Chino, Nagano|en|Chino, Nagano|qid=Q838660|lt=Chino, Nagano}}.<ref>{{Cite book|author=Yamada Shūmoku|title=Tenpaku Kiryō|year=2016|publisher=Ningensha|page=147}}</ref>

== Shrines ==
* '''Tenpaku Shime Shrine''' (天白七五三社) ({{ill|Chino, Nagano|en|Chino, Nagano|qid=Q838660|lt=Chino, Nagano}})
*** Recognized as the original dwelling of Yatsuka-o-no-Mikoto. It is considered the main shrine of the 28 Tenpaku shrines in the Suwa region.<ref>{{Cite book|author=Yamada Shūmoku|title=Tenpaku Kiryō|year=2016|publisher=Ningensha|pages=143-144}}</ref>
* '''{{ill|Tatsuya-Sukura Shrine|ja|達屋酢蔵神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tatsuya-Sukura Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}''' ({{ill|Chino, Nagano|en|Chino, Nagano|qid=Q838660|lt=Chino, Nagano}})
*** A merged shrine of Tatsuya and Sukura, both subordinate shrines of Suwa Taisha Upper Shrine.
* '''Dai-Tenpaku Shrine''' ({{ill|Chino, Nagano|en|Chino, Nagano|qid=Q838660|lt=Chino, Nagano}})
*** The tutelary shrine of the Oyajima family. The main deity is Yatsuka-o-no-Mikoto, among other gods. The shrine's main hall, built in 1850 by the famed sculptor [[Tatekawa Washirō Tomimasa]], is designated as a cultural property of [[Chino City]].<ref>Dai-Tenpaku Shrine signboard.</ref>
